title: First N Squares
description:
Write a function `first_n_squares(n)` that returns a list of squares of the first `n` positive integers, starting from 1 up to and including `n` (i.e. [1, 4, 9, ...]).
If `n <= 0`, return an empty list `[]`.
hints: Python range() starts at 0 by default and excludes the upper bound.
Inspect the start and end arguments passed to range(): does your loop begin at 0 or 1?
If you write range(n), your loop generates 0 through n-1, starting with 0^2 and missing n^2.
Use range(1, n + 1) to generate integers strictly from 1 through n inclusive.
